back: For ax² + bx + c = 0: x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)]/(2a). Example: x² + 2x − 8 = 0 gives x = 2 or −4.
If aᶠ⁽ˣ⁾ = aᵍ⁽ˣ⁾ then f(x) = g(x). Example: 5^(x²+2x−6) = 25 gives x² + 2x − 8 = 0.
ln(xᵏ) = k·ln x; ln(ab) = ln a + ln b; ln(a/b) = ln a − ln b.
3ln(x⁴) + 3ln(x²) = 54 gives 18 ln x = 54, so ln x = 3 and x = e³.
e^(ln x) = x (x > 0) and ln(eˣ) = x. Use one to undo the other.

front: Limit at infinity of a rational function
back: Compare the highest powers. (x⁴ + ...)/(−4x⁴ + ...) tends to 1/(−4) = −1/4 as x → ±∞.
d/dx xⁿ = n·xⁿ⁻¹. Example: √(x³) = x^(3/2) has derivative (3/2)x^(1/2).
y − f(a) = f′(a)(x − a). For f = √(x³) at x = 16: f = 64, f′ = 6, so y = 6x − 32.
(u·v)′ = u′v + uv′. Example: (x² − 15)eˣ has derivative eˣ(x² + 2x − 15).
(u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v². Example: f = (2x − 5)/ln x gives f′(2) ≈ 3.926.
[f(g(x))]′ = f′(g(x))·g′(x): differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the inner derivative.

front: Derivatives of eˣ and ln x
back: (eˣ)′ = eˣ and (ln x)′ = 1/x.
f″(x) > 0: convex (curving up). f″(x) < 0: concave. For ax³ + ln x at x = 1, f″ = 6a − 1 > 0 gives a > 1/6.
TR = P·Q, MR = dTR/dQ, AR = TR/Q (equals P). With P = 400 − 4Q: MR = 400 − 8Q.
f′ > 0: increasing. f′ < 0: decreasing. Check the sign of f′ between its roots.
f′ changes + to −: local max. f′ changes − to +: local min. Example: eˣ(x + 5)(x − 3) has max at x = −5, min at x = 3.
f′(x*) = 0 and f″(x*) < 0: local max; f″(x*) > 0: local min.
TP = TR − TC; set TP′ = 0 and check TP″ < 0. TP = −5Q² + 100Q − 72 gives Q = 10 and TP = 428.
A continuous function on a closed bounded interval [a, b] attains a maximum and a minimum.
A point where concavity changes: f″ changes sign.
∫xⁿdx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C (n ≠ −1); ∫eˣdx = eˣ + C; ∫(1/x)dx = ln|x| + C.
∫u dv = uv − ∫v du. Choose u to be a function that gets simpler when differentiated.
∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b) − F(a): area under the curve if f ≥ 0. Area between curves: ∫(upper − lower)dx.
∂f/∂x: differentiate with respect to x, treating the other variables as constants.
∇f = (∂f/∂x, ∂f/∂y): points in the direction of steepest increase of f.
Solve fₓ = 0 and f_y = 0 together. Classify with the Hessian (second-order partials).
Optimize f(x, y) subject to g(x, y) = c with L = f − λ(g − c). Set partials of L to 0. λ is the shadow price.
n! orders n items. Arrangements: n!/(n − k)!. Combinations: C(n, k) = n!/[k!(n − k)!].
